sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for PDF diagnostic tests
sections.what: Brings in logging, the PDF writer, the PDF module under test, and the cancel error type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests check how PDF parser warnings are captured.

sections.name: test_parser_warnings_retained_without_claiming_source_fidelity
sections.title: Parser warnings kept without claiming fidelity
sections.what: A parser warning during extraction is recorded in the result, and the first page is flagged for visual review with a note that page attribution is unavailable. The temporary handler is removed afterwards.
sections.why: Likely reason: parser warnings mean text may be incomplete, so a person should check the page.
sections.watch_out: Warned pages must not be described as faithfully read, and the review flag is what this test protects.

sections.name: test_parser_diagnostic_storage_is_bounded
sections.title: Diagnostic storage stays bounded
sections.what: Sends a thousand long warnings to the capture and checks that all are counted but only sixty-four are kept, each shortened.
sections.why: Likely reason: a broken PDF can produce huge numbers of warnings, which must not fill memory.
sections.watch_out: The sixty-four limit is fixed in this test's expectations.

sections.name: test_parser_diagnostic_handler_removed_after_failure
sections.title: Capture removed after failure
sections.what: When extraction fails, the temporary warning handler is removed so later logging is not affected.
sections.why: Likely reason: a leftover handler would keep capturing logs for the rest of the program.
sections.watch_out: Any new early exit must still run this cleanup.

sections.name: test_diagnostic_receipt_survives_failure_and_cancellation
sections.title: Diagnostic receipt kept on failure or cancel
sections.what: When a PDF fails or is cancelled after a parser warning, the receipt still lists that warning with its level, and the original error or cancel is re-raised unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a person can see why the file failed.
sections.watch_out: The original exception must be re-raised, not wrapped in a new one.

sections.name: test_normal_logging_preserved_without_cross_thread_capture_or_duplicates
sections.title: Normal logging kept, no duplicates or cross-thread capture
sections.what: Checks that ordinary logging still reaches the configured output exactly once, and that the capture counts only warnings produced on its own thread, with the same behaviour whether or not logging is configured.
sections.why: Likely reason: the capture must not steal or double other programs' logs.
sections.watch_out: The thread check reads an internal record field, so a change in Python's logging internals could affect it.

summary: Tests that PDF parser warnings are captured, bounded, cleaned up, and reported without disturbing normal logging.
purpose: Makes sure a broken PDF's warnings are kept as evidence for a reviewer and that the capture does not leak or duplicate other logs.
why: Likely reason: PDF parsers can emit many warnings, and these mean text may be incomplete. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
how: Each test installs a fake warning, runs the PDF extraction or the capture object directly, and checks the stored messages, counts, the review flag, and that the temporary handler was removed.
inputs: Small generated PDFs, fake log records, and replacement functions for the extraction steps.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No lasting files are written.
risks: The thread test depends on an internal logging field, so changes in Python's logging could affect it.
debug: Check the failing test name, then the captured message list and whether the handler is still attached to the pypdf logger.
